newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK frenzy-buying creates record "red-chip" bonanza.
newsitem.headline: HK frenzy-buying creates record "red-chip" bonanza.

text.p: A share-buying frenzy by investors seeking a stake in Beijing city government-linked business has touched off a spectacular "red-chip" bonanza breaking all Hong Kong records.
The unprecedented investment surge by Hong Kong capitalists -- big and small - was disclosed on Wednesday, 34 days before the British colony becomes a special region of communist-ruled China.

Cashing in on investors' enthusiasm for one of the world's fastest-growing economies, red-chip conglomerate Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd has taken Hong Kong by storm ahead of the territory's return to China.
It announced the highest subscription level ever for an initial public offering and debut trading on Thursday is likely to be huge.
The China-backed company, an investment arm of the capital's municipality, said its Hong Kong offering was a massive 1,276 times subscribed, a record here.

Applications for a total 17.22 billion shares flooded in last week, tying up more than HK$200 billion (US$ 26 billion) in Hong Kong's banking system until unsuccessful applicants get their cheques back.
"We are very pleased to see the enthusiastic response to the company's share issue," chairman Hu Zhao Guang said.

In a development that would have confounded communism's founding father Karl Marx, the term red chip has now joined the capitalist world's blue chip to describe highly-fancied stocks from the People's Republic.
In extraordinary scenes, thousands of people -- many first-time stock investors -- descended on local banks last week to apply for shares.

Beijing Enterprises launched its share offer last Tuesday amid an existing craze in Hong Kong for red chip stocks before the territory returns to Chinese rule on July 1. Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China.
GITIC Enterprises Ltd, also a red chip, held the previous subscription record. Its issue in March was 892 times subscribed.

Beijing Enterprises offered 13.5 million shares to the Hong Kong public and a further 1.5 million to employees as part of a global 150 million share initial public offering. A total 324,754 valid application forms were received for the public offering, 75 percent of which were for 6,000 shares or less.
Beijing Enterprises said the overwhelming response prompted it to boost its retail offering, with 51.75 million shares finally allocated the Hong Kong public and company employees.

Major companies are also in on the act, with Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd , Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, New World Development Co Ltd, Kerry Holdings Ltd, Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd, Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd and America's Morgan Stanley Group Inc together holding six percent of the company.
Beijing Holdings Ltd will hold 69 percent.
The craze surrounding Beijing Enterprises stems from its ties to the Beijing municipal government and hopes that the parent will inject valuable assets into its unit in the future.
Beijing Enterprises has interests in consumer products manufacturing, infrastructure, services and high-technology.
The company owns a stake in Beijing McDonald's, the company which operates the fast-food chain in the city. It is also involved in brewing, toll roads, hotels and retailing.
Brokers expect the stock to skyrocket on Thursday, with the unofficial market price quoted around HK$40 (US$ 5) on Wednesday compared with an issue price of HK$12.48 (US$ 1.60).
Beijing Enterprises has said the issue would raise net proceeds of about HK$2.19 billion (US$ 283 million).
